cells.tense: The exchange is being kept level right now, and you are the one keeping it.
cells.ask: At the end of today, count one thing you gave and one you got back, and let the number stand without adjusting it.
cells.core:
Giving and receiving are running about even here. You pick up when a room has tilted and you add or ease off before anyone says anything, and that adjustment happens fast enough that it doesn't register as a decision. It isn't a middle you parked on. It's a line you find again after the ground moves.

What people hand back to you arrives, and letting it arrive is its own kind of skill. So the ask is small: at the end of today, count one thing you gave and one you got back, and let the number stand without adjusting it. Whatever the count says is information, not a verdict. Nothing about it needs fixing tonight.
cells.sheetLine: You keep the give and take level without making a show of it.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead you can see an exchange coming out uneven, and you are already dosing your giving against it.
cells.ask: Pick one person and let the next thing you give them go uncounted, with nothing owed back this week.
cells.core:
You're managing the exchange before it happens. Not generosity — calculation. You know roughly what you're owed, roughly what you owe, and you're measuring both out ahead of time so nobody comes out short. Fairness has turned into a job you do in advance, and you're doing it with friends.

It reads as care from outside. From inside it's a squeeze, because no exchange can ever close at the number you set. So the ask is the small way out: pick one person and let the next thing you give them go uncounted, with nothing owed back this week. You don't have to stop knowing what things cost. You just don't have to settle the account tonight.

cells.tense: The exchange came apart a while back, and you stopped counting yourself in from there.
cells.ask: Name what you need from one person, in a plain sentence, and let it sit there without softening it.
cells.core:
There's an exchange you stopped taking part in. Not a decision anyone made out loud — giving and getting got tangled with something that didn't come out even, and you stepped back from the whole activity. Now you're in rooms where people are passing things around and your hands stay down.

Generosity isn't the gap. You still give. What's gone is the other half — letting something come toward you and keeping it. So here's something small: name what you need from one person, in a plain sentence, and let it sit there without softening it. Whatever comes back, you can say yes or no. The point is to be inside the exchange again, not to get it right.

cells.tense: You are already keeping this fair right now, and you describe it as just how things worked out.
cells.ask: When you notice yourself evening something out today, say once that you did it.
cells.core:
When something's off balance between people, you move on it — you take the smaller share, you cover the gap, you say the thing that puts someone back on their feet. It runs all day and you don't call it anything. It was what happened to be needed, so you did it.

That's the part worth seeing. The fairness is real and the account of it is written in the passive voice, as if it happened to you. So try this once: when you notice yourself evening something out today, say once that you did it. Not out loud to the room necessarily — just once, in your own words, owned. The action won't change. What's being left on the table is the fact that it was yours.
